review_description: SolarShop failed to advise us that the mounts needed to be more than 5m from the point of connection (a local utility requirement!), so we had to dig another set of mount holes. They DID, however, split the cost of the digger for the second set. Installation was efficiently done, once the mounts were in place.With ground mount, and a short run to the meter box, we maximised FiT while it was available on gross metering. Downside was that, with the requirement to changeover to Net metering, we lose a bit in the generation run (as the panels are around 200m from house).Install was 3 strings of 10, 60W panels = 1.8kW, mounted on ground frames.

Solar shop were great I was able to do everything over the phone and email including sending photos which was great considering my time restrictions and rural location. Matt was very helpful and extremely knowledgeable.Your web site was a great starting point so I had a better understanding and could talk with knowledge to the sales reps.
The main reason for choosing this product was that I have some shading issues and these panels are meant to be better in these conditions.
I was made a lot of promises about when the system would be up and running which proved to be unrealistic

Obtaining an installation date was difficult;The notifying of the electrical authority and arranging power meter change was not done (according to the authority)- fortunately I checked and was able to have this effected.The panels did not fit the roof space requiring the installers to be delayed, they did find a compromise after a few hours delay.The installers were good.

The Solar Shop rep was responsive and very attentive to my needs and visited me personally when I had additional queries. Excellent customer service. Whilst I certainly appreciated this sites (your) assistance and advice, I found that the organisations that you recommended to be very unresponsive and if that is their approach to business and potential clients then I would suggest that their installations / workmanship would have to be closely observed. Thanks for your help tho.

We had quite a bit of technical information then some suppliers told us to choose from that.  It's like choosing a mobile phone plan - far too much complicated information.  Warren asked us what we wanted from our system, then gave us choices with prices to match our wants.  He then explained the difference between the choices offered.  It's difficult to match prices to other suppliers as we didn't get quotes or even anyone to come to our house to help us decide.  We had one phone call and some email responses which asked a lot of questions that we didn't really know the answers to, such as roof size and which type and how many panels we preferred.  Even though our system is not installed yet, we feel happy with our choice of supplier as do some of our friends and neighbours who used The Solar Shop.  Prices compare reasonably with other friends for smaller systems from other companies.

They had everything organized.  They did a room inspection prior to installation and discussed best possible location.The system was installed on a Friday and immediately got the new meter on a Monday - FAB!  I have a friend who took 6 months to get a meter as the electrician did no file the paperwork.Face to Face people discussed my needs, what I wanted and gave me the information to make an informed decision.However, still enjoy reading your website, email updates etc.

The property assessor for our area was friendly, knowledgeable, assessing the best type of system we were able to install at the best price. He provided us with much of the information we needed and also the answers to our questions.The recommended inverter and panels were better quality systems than a previous quote.However, being a reputable larger company meant that there is a time delay before instillation can occur - our system will not be installed until August.

I THINK that I got a good value system but it won't be installed until 14 July and not grid connected untill ????? So time will tell, if you send me  a survey  in a month or three I'll be in a better position to answer.

We went with  Solarshop1.  Because they are an established business of some 9 years.2.Salesman was extremely helpfull, and we did not feel 'pressured' as happened with one of the others.3.  With the problems with Japan being their supplier, they  had to change panels to make sure we were in time with our installation, and we ended up with a better deal.Not sure of the  kW, but have 35 - 60w panels coming.

Company is currently in receivership which has made the process quite stressful and harder than necessary. The quality of the installer and the electricity supplier have jaded up for this significantly.

Let me say from the outset I was very happy with your input and assistance in addition to the information you made available on your web site, it was all very useful. You were let down somewhat by your referrals.I do not intend to criticise the two contractors you made reference to but suffice to say they leave a lot to be desired. Trades people do not necessarily make good sales personnel and vice versa. I went with the SolarShop, not on price but rather on presentation, openness, assistance and documentation.Thank you sincerely for your help it was /is  much appreciated.

System hasn't been installed as yet but meter changeover to take place next week.Service levels seem to be right on track with installation to be completed within 3 months from signing up - just in time for summer.

Adelaide Solar Systems were quite good as long as I knew what I wanted. However, of the many companies I spoke too the Solarshop was the only company interested in answering the many technical and system physical questions I had. The others were only interested in installing a system that in their words "will do the job;. I want to be electrically neutral not have a system that; should; or will;probably; reduce electricity bills for most of the year. My system will be installed mid December 2010.Am I confident that I have chosen the right system??? all my investigations of the many systems on the market say I should be.But of course I won't know that until about this time next year.
Good follow-up from the Company to date. Keep us informed on the steps involved & progress of our application.

Although I got some quotes from Todae Solar and Nichol's, I've decided to go with Solarshop as they have the product that is more suitable for my roof and also they have Japanese brand which I believe better looking (cosmetically) than the Chinese brands. Apart from that the quote's I've got from your supplier were quiet competitive but if I had to choose between Todae Solar and Nichol's I'd go for Todae as they took the time to come over and explain the options. Whereas Nichol's just sent me email for the quotes based on the picture they've got from Google map which is very old.

Solar Shop insisted on an onsite visit before quoting which gave me some assurance the system would be suitable and adjusted preformance accordingly. Their final price was as good as the internet only company prices.

The price differences were quite large but I preferred to go with a supplier with local presence.  I did not like their xantrex inverters so have asked them to organise a German one without a transformer.
Barbara Hutton was particularly good & amp;  was helpful & amp; detached in a remarkable fashion

THE INSTALLERS : The installers were excellent and did a high quality job, leaving me with a very professional finished product. They answered all my questions and their knowledge of the system was of expert level.THE SUPPLIERS : I found myself putting pressure on the suppliers to keep the installation on track with the date promised at the time of sale. In the end the system was installed and commissioned about a week after initially stated.

The reality is the quality of the product and the choice of panel, because I live on a corner in a high visiblity area, looks was the major factor, thats why I went for the black panel as they looked smart. I can't wait to see them on the roof
Not installed yet so would like to review answers when it gets done

The system is great. Installation was delayed because supply could not keep up with demand. The only negative was that we were not told that we had to organise getting the Gross Feed Meter connected through our own electrician. Had we been told this we would have booked him to come the day after installation. We had to wait a month for meters to become available.

My install was scheduled for 22/12/9 but ended up on 22/4/2010, 4 months late. was at first due to shortage of inverers then they arrived and they had no panels then panels available but no inverters, then eventually they got them both.By this time I was very worried about how my install would go, but turned out they all seemed to be good at their job and all works well. Whew!!Solar Shop did it and they reduced the quote by $750 to allow for lost power production over the 4 months. Found it a bit difficult to deal with a company 450km from me but got there in the end
I should have waited six months and got better value for my dollar.

There was some lack of communication and some issues which has meant it's been 5 months from my initial consultation to installation (still waiting on gross feed-in meter to be installed - hopefully in the next week or so).Main issue is that I have a steel frame roof and even though I made this clear many times the original attempt to install couldn't go ahead as bracket fixing method was not suitable.Had to wait a further month, but am satisified with method now used.BUT the electrician didn't complete the install for a further month after that. Each time I had to chase them for information and then not all the information was complete.The workmanship seems excellent, but the delay and some aspects of the service were/are dissappointing.
I had two quotes, one from Solar Shop, who I went with and one from Zen.Both were good but I ended up going for the thin film panel due to better performance in shade.
Amorphous Crystalline System - 42 panels 4.65 kWBest operation in higher temperatures as seen on the Desert Solar Centre websiteAlso can get 10 Fly Buys points for every dollar spent

Wasn't happy with SA Quality Home Improvements at all.  Took a followup to get someone out and then never actually received a quote!Solar Shop was excellent to deal with. Very happy with the entire experience.
Bit concerned because it was a big TV ad that drew me in but happy with it all the way, now working beautifully.
Sales Rep explained how to get most value for money and how we would pay for the system through energy use profiling and not FIT or rebates etc.

The professionalism and depth of knowledge left nothing to be desired, Solar Shop was able to answer every question put to them with much depth.They knew and understood the entire process from me signing to the actual commissioning of the system. Unfortunately, the sales person did not make it clear to me that in Victoria there was a likely wait of two months from installation time to commissioning.I challenged Solar Shop on this as for the two month period there was to be a no return on investment and this was to be my financial problem, to which I said that this was not acceptable. I challenged Solar Shop on this and now we will both share the financial burden of a waiting period between installation and commissioning.I will make a part payment at installation and then pay the balance at the time of commissioning.

I found the whole experience rather daunting, with so many new companies coming on the market it is very dificult to decide which way to go. I finally decided to go with a known company rather than take a chance with an unknown company. Hopefully it is the right decision!
Gave complete advise in an area where useful information is hard to find.
We looked up the equipment and went with what we thought was the best value to us.Also, the Solarshop came recommended from a friend who was happy with them.

Very positive interaction with the salesperson, referred by word of mouth.  Good 'briefing' and understanding of requirements.  No BS, facts nor 'push' given the current climate.  Realistic advice and quote.

The system was installed 18 months ago and prices have decreased since then. The price was good at the time and qualified for the FIT of 50.05 c/kWhr.The salesman lacked technical knowledge (he wanted to use a single tracking inverter for panels on both the north and west facing roofs, wanted to use 60 watt panels and suggested a 1kW.I told him he didn't understand the physics of photovoltaics and embarrassed him into the same size system using 180 watt panels for the same price as the 60 watt panels they have been programmed to flog.Thanks for the seven energy saving tips.RegardsMark
Whilst a little more expensive overall, their finance plans were excellent and that is what sold us in the end.

So far I can recommend the Solar Shop based on our experience. We did get a quote from another company which was set up in the middle of a shopping centre and they were quite a bit more expensive. This has been a bit of a minefield for us because there are so many companies out there. What helped was doing our own research first and working out the differences in panel types and where the quality components come from.

It would have been useful to have the state/region of the installer in the "Solar Installer Reviews" page.  That way we may have been able to look a little closer at other installers in our area.Other than that, you have provided us with tons of information and follow up in a timely fashion.Not that all the suppliers/installers we contacted have done the same :-(Thank you for a great service.
System not installed yet.Good efficiency panels - quick quotes - discount for paying in full up front even by credit card. Very good customer service. Very good referral from a friend. Not pushy.

This company was very thorough and go by the book regarding council regulations and explained all aspects of the installation and equipment. They have also already organized the change over of the meter by the electricity company.They also have the opportunity of finance for the system.The one thing really impressed me was they came to my property and assessed it and followed through with my quotes, more than I can say for some of the other companies. Some I am still waiting for the quotes.

I went with this system because it Japanese &  German made . One thing I must say  I was very happy with Assured Class Electrical Quote the only reason  I did not go with them was it was Chinese But his quote was good and it was in booklet form & was  done Best Ive seen
I think there are a lot of ill informed sales people trying to sell solar panels and unfortunately the info given by them did not add up and was somewhat conflicting.

As I did not have a lot of time to choose between suppliers. I felt the ones who could come out and see me were the preferred option.It was good to get quotes online, and the businesses that responded did well and also kept in contact. I ended up going with a local supplier who could guarantee me installation by June. Thank you for your recommendations. They helped with my research into solar power.

Also had a quote from SolarGain.  Was not impressed by the service from SolarGain, the salesperson wasn't interested and didn't even follow up.Decided to go with the hybrid system with solar shop but still waiting for it to be installed.

Following my request to your website, I was only contacted by one company (Renewable Logic) who did send a consultant out who took our details and measurements and promised to provide a written quote the next day.  Almost 2 months later we haven't heard back from them.  So we went with SolarShop following feedback from friends who had used them - not installed as yet due to panels being delayed by the Japanese earthquake.
They did the job . No one else could match price or would take it on in Broome.

I found the Solar Shop Riverland representative to be honest with his answers to my questions (there were a lot of questions I asked) and the representative was the only one to actually sit down with my wife and I. And show us the ins & outs and positives and negatives of what we were going to purchase. The representative even suggested putting some panels on the shed which I hadn't even thought of. So all in all it has been a great experience so far.

We decided on using an amorphous system as opposed to the mono-crystalline as relatives have been using this type and they have been getting excellent results with a 3 Kilowatt system for about two years now. Very few companies are using the amorphous type of panel, however we have seen the results and also like the fact that panels are made in Japan - [ as opposed to mono-crystalline which are mostly Chinese manufactured.]
I feel like once we signed and paid the deposit we were forgotten.  We got different responses from our sales person versus the actual company on install dates which was really dissappointing.

I have worked in the renewable energy area for a while and chose the solar shop as I have had previous contact with them through my work.  I know that their systems have all been tested to Australian Standard, as we did do some of their testing (for solar hot water systems).  I also did choose the Solar Shop as they are a local Adelaide company that has now expanded nationally.  This gives me piece of mind that they will be around to honour any warranty issues, unlike some of the other companies that are appearing now - they werenââ‚¬â„¢t here yesterday, so will they still be here tomorrow when issues arise?  A solar shop representative actually came out and did a site visit - some of the companies that I asked for quotes from would only do a site visit after you paid the deposit, all very suspect in my eyes.  The other deciding factor in choosing the Solar Shop was the fact that they rang me maybe 30 mins after I sent the email to arrange a time for a site visit, they have called me back promptly when I had queries and my quote arrived within 2 days of the visit.  Some of the companies I emailed I haven't had any response from yet.

The one item that stands out most of all is the fact that not one company can quote the same items or size and so price justifacation between companies can be confusing without even getting to the installation side of it.If people are looking for better quality panels then the price gets dearer and this is where it becomes difficult.I went with a friend who works in the industry to supply my 2 systems. Both 1.8kw units with good quality panels. In the end it was better to put faith in somebody I know than to just fork out a large amount of cash to somebody I didnt know.Having said all that somebody is making plenty of money from all this solar hype. I dont expect you to print this

After shopping around and listening to what each company had to say and looking up as much as I could on the internet, I decided to buy from a company that was well established, just in case I need to have anything fixed through warranty later. I also made sure I had quality components in my order to allow the best results.

Your information was very helpful and I took your advice re: buying a useage meter which was most helpful and informative. The combination of finding the hybrid panels plus reducing our useage meant that it was economically viable as well as environmentally attractive to proceed. Thank you!

System not yet installed as needed to get a DA approved by local council and this has taken time and money - $300 for DA + $550 for structural engineers cert that roof would support panels (700kg total but only 17 kg/sqm). Still waiting for formal sign-off from council (but just verbally approved) and the electricity network supplier has also now approved installation so this is scheduled for early in the New Year..

Always get at least 3 quotes.I actually saw 5 companies. Do some research on the companies you will be seeing. Check out reviews/forums on the internet regarding solar panels.There is a website www.desertknowledge.com.au, the first site in Australia to publicly showcase such a broad range of large scale solar installations including panels made internationally. Ensure you get a 10yr Inverter warranty, some only offer 5yrs. 3 of the 5 companies, preferred to send a quote to you. The other 2 provided on-spot quotes which we were able to negotiate a better deal when you talk money.I found the experience quite daunting, so I roped my husband in on the last 3 meetings, it was a godsend. My best advice, get the system you want that will best suit your needs and stick to it, don't rely too heavily on the sales rep convincing you what you should get.

Only 1 of the people through your system contacted me. I was very happy with them but in the end it came down to price and what I thought was the best system in my situation.I received two other quotes from businesses that I contacted myself.
No follow up on the gov't changes. Left to my own devices to sort it all out.

It was a toss of the coin whether I went with Solar Wholesalers or Solar Shop - I went Solar Shop due to others in the area having used their product (thin film) and suggesting they were the better product. Their sales rep also visited twice to explain his product.I would like to make special mention of Andrew Sendy CEO from Solar Wholesalers, if had I not spoken to others in the local community that had the thin film product I would have definitely gone with Solar Wholesalers as Andrew was super helpful and not at all pushy - his product seemed as good as the thin film product as far as I could work out from reading all the information on the web and it was about $800 cheaper.Finn, I would also like to make mention of all the help and information that you put forward for me to help me make my dicission, it was very much appreciated.

Of the 3 companies approach SolarShop provided the best and most comprehensive advice.  The rep was prepared to spend considerable time assessing the site and explaining about the type of panels recommended.  One Company, TRU Energy, my supplier was quite good but did the whole assessment and quote over the phone and using Google maps.  The 3rd company, Regency Energy, although sending a rep did not follow up and the person did not seem to have much knowledge or experience in the field.Having committed what for us is a lot of money to this project, I sometimes wonder about the wisdom.  It is possibly more effective to invest the money in a company supplying renewable energy like a wind farm.  One advice I have received suggest home PV systems are relatively inefficient use of resources and means of generating electricity compared to investing in a wind farm.It has only been a couple of weeks since signing up and installtion is likely to be some weeks off.  I have also just received a letter from SolarShop indicating a supply problem 9shortage) of PV panels which will further delay installation.

I also had advice and assistance from a close friend who has had a 2-year experience of owning a solar system supplied and fitted by a different installer.With your list and her experience we knew which questions to ask, and were satisfied with the answers.Difficult to fully evaluate my installer at this stage, with no installation up.
Thank you for your lead for us. This was the start of a very involved process with all the various types of systems on the market.
Only one person called me from the 3 quotes you promised.  I was very disappointed.
We are not connected to the grid yet. When we connect to the grid I will send you more information.

Choosing supplier and type of panel was initially confusing. An acquaintance recommended Solar Shop but they were already on my list to contact. The sales person was thorough in his explanation of the different types of panels and had clear brochures to follow that up. Prices of all the different types and sizes were tabulated. You knew you got what you were paying for. I also felt confident in this deal as this company have been doing this work for a number of years, and their reputation was at stake. The installation was done three weeks after payment due to an unexpected cancellation by someone else - otherwise we would still be waiting due to the big demand. The work was inspected a week later and now we are waiting on the power company to install a new meter.

Was very good with communication and explained everything to us fully, with the total cost. The price we were given has no more hidden charges we do not have to contact any electricians as it is all done for us. Found Reg to be very thorough and helpful. Everything was explained to us and they did not hassle us for a decision , we were told to contact them when we made a decision. I like the fact that there was no pressure from them
See above comment.
The system still hasn't been installed yet. It is being approved by local council at the present.

Thank you for your attempts to find us a local supplier. I used your guide for items to look out for and found it very useful. A local fellow did come and quote but did not follow up. I had to contact him for a written quote that contain no details about the different cells (quality and/or origin). I had to chase him a number of times and thought that this was a bad omen so started to look around for another supplier.We ended up going with Solar shop (they were recommended by a family friend) who actually convinced us to go for a larger system than we first intended. I was impressed with their professionalism, their willingness to offer options and to explain the merits of various technologies. The system is not installed yet but if you want more feedback I am happy to supply it.

the sales person from the Solar Shop was  very informative and wasn't pushy in any way . I can not say the same with the rep from Ecoplus . I would like you to get back to me further down the track to see weather i think solar power on a 1.6 kw system was worth the expense .

I had a few dodgy salesmen come, which was a bit weird. One guy had no idea about what he was selling - I knew more than he did (which wasn't much); one classic thing he said was " our system is better because it's polycrystalline in structure" ... he followed this without a pause by adding "...and I don't know what the hell that means" !!!!! Needless to say he didn't get the job. Gave it to solarshop guy as he was by far the most professional, didn't oversell his product and didn't just try to jam the biggest system he could on my roof. Hope that helps...feel free to use my comments.Alan.NSW

A little disappointing in that could not supply original system quoted but kept us informed. Installation delay was greater than expected. Otherwise very happy with service and would use them again ir required.
We have purchased a system but it will not be installed until September due to shortage of panels (high demand)

Although they could not supply the original panels due to a supplier problem, they gave us a two option alternative if we did not wish to wait on the original panels. We chose a different option of the same if not better output and it was installed within a week of adjusting the contract with better credits.
Very good onsite planning and explanation regarding system and installationThe only hold up has been waiting for supply of gross feed-in meters

I had quite a delay from when I payed my deposit to my actual installation date, due to a shortage of inverters, (approx 5 months). However I am very pleased now that my solar installation is operating. It is averaging around 10 KW per day, so far. I haven't received a power bill yet but it should be significantly reduced for the next quarter.
The system that we have is making more power than we expected or anticipated.
Most people would find that it is just too hard a road to go down!

Had a very good sales person all information given on the initial day and also gave a aerial view  of the house with panels superimposed onto it.Fantastic product information in regards to panels various types for cloudy /shady areas inverters also .Break down of costs associated with our previous electricity bill and future savings to be made with panels installed of our choosing as had a vast array of panels available .Installation was a breeze came early and on time approximately 3-4 hrs to install panels then sparkie did his  initial wiring 2hrs finished the next morning and turned on after new meter was installed
Actually still not yet installed. Shortage of the Hybrid Kanaeca panels.
I was part of a group scheme in the north eastern suburbs.
Would not go with anyone else but solarshop.

I had a long wait (3months) from deposit being paid to installation. This was due to a shortage of inverters in Australia. I decided to pay a little more and get the best panels that were suitable for my limited size roof. The Sanyo 210w panels seem to be very efficient. I have A SB 3800 inverter with 14 panels that give me a 2.94kW system. Soon I will be installing another 6 Panels on another roof with a SB 1700 inverter. This will give me a total of 4.2kW
